response: Yes, dermatomyositis and polymyositis can affect similar thigh muscles. Both conditions are types of inflammatory myopathies that can cause muscle weakness and inflammation in the proximal muscles, including those in the thighs. The specific thigh muscles that may be affected include the quadriceps, hamstrings, and hip flexors. However, dermatomyositis is also characterized by skin rash and other skin manifestations, whereas polymyositis primarily affects the muscles without skin involvement.
